en.title: Maps and signs
en.summary: How to read street maps, compass directions and the signs you see in a town.

paragraphs: Maps and signs use short, fixed language. In this lesson you will learn the compass points, the common words on public signs, and how to compare distances.
Two friends are standing in front of a map of York city centre.

lines.speaker: Ella
lines.text: Where are we on the map?

lines.speaker: Finn
lines.text: We are here, next to the river. The cathedral is to the north.

lines.speaker: Finn
lines.text: It is in the south-west, about a kilometre away. Look, there is a sign: Station, 800 metres.

lines.speaker: Ella
lines.text: Is that sign right? It looks closer on the map.

lines.speaker: Finn
lines.text: The map is not drawn to scale, so you cannot trust the distances.

lines.speaker: Ella
lines.text: Then let us follow the signs. They are easier to read than the map.

lines.speaker: Finn
lines.text: Good idea. We can walk along the river and then cross the bridge.

paragraphs: **1. The compass points give direction and combine.** Use in the north, to the north of, or an adjective such as northern. A combination such as south-west is written with a hyphen. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives.

blocks.html:
FormExample
in the north / southThe cathedral is in the north of the city.
to the east ofThe park is to the east of the station.
north-westThe castle is in the north-west.
northern, southernthe northern bridge

paragraphs: **2. Signs are short.** They drop articles and verbs, and they use fixed words. Understanding the shortened pattern helps you read quickly. See Introduction to Grammar: Sentence structure.

blocks.html:
SignMeaning
Exitthe way out
No entryyou may not go in
Give waylet other traffic pass first
Keep leftstay on the left side
Road closedyou cannot drive here

items: A scale such as 1:25,000 means one unit on the map equals 25,000 on the ground.
A one-way street allows traffic in only one direction.
Pedestrian means a person on foot, and a pedestrian crossing is a place to cross the road.
A map key or legend explains the symbols.

paragraphs: In Britain and the United States distances on road signs are in miles, although many local signs for walkers also give kilometres or metres. Bus stops in British towns often show a small map with the words You are here.
